title: Telemetry Gate & Evidence Fanout — Collector Guidance and Runbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc defines the Telemetry Gate pattern (an ingest-time gatekeeper), the evidence fanout semantics for automated collectors, and the operational runbook for ensuring high-confidence evidence delivery to downstream SIEM/export systems. Focus is on low-latency proof collection that preserves chain-of-custody, supports RBAC v2 constraints, and remains resilient under bursty load.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: security engineers, SREs, infra engineers building collectors, compliance owners, and solutions engineers who integrate exports with customer SIEMs.
- Scope: collector-side behavior, ingest gating rules, envelope format, fanout policies, checkpointing/idempotency, SIEM mapping guidance, and incident/runbook steps. This does NOT cover long-term retention replication or forensics indexing (separate doc).

High-level overview (one-liner):
Telemetry Gate = light fingerprinting + policy decision point that accepts, enriches, and routes evidence to fanout queues with strong provenance headers and retryable semantics.

Architecture (conceptual):
- Collector (edge) -> Telemetry Gate (ingest cluster) -> Evidence Ledger (durable queue + checkpoint store) -> Fanout Worker pool -> Target sinks (SIEM exports, control-evidence store, long-term archive)
- Auxiliary: KeyManager (KMS/HSM) for signing provenance, RBAC service for token validation, Observability collector for telemetry metrics.

Design goals and constraints:
- Minimal latency on critical evidence (sub-100ms goal for control signals).
- Idempotent delivery to each sink.
- Signed provenance metadata at ingest time.
- Policy-driven routing (customer, control type, severity).
- Respect RBAC v2: collectors only operate with scoped service identities.
- Backpressure handling and graceful degradation to keep system online while preserving evidence fidelity.

Telemetry Gate responsibilities (detailed):
1) Authenticate & authorize incoming collector requests using RBAC v2 tokens.
2) Validate envelope schema and apply lightweight schema normalization.
3) Compute a deterministic evidence_key (hash) for idempotency.
4) Attach provenance headers: signed_digest, ingested_by, ingest_ts, origin_checksum.
5) Apply routing policies: immediate-fanout, prioritized-fanout, deferred-archive.
6) Emit ingest metrics (success/failure/latency) and a small sampling of raw events for QA.
7) Persist a small checkpoint record to Evidence Ledger (not whole payload).

Envelope schema (informal example, exact JSON schema lives in Confluence):
{
  "envelope_version": "v2",
  "evidence_type": "control-action|access-event|config-change",
  "evidence_id": "<client-generated-uuid-or-key-hash>",
  "evidence_key": "sha256(<payload>)",
  "collector_id": "edge-collector-23",
  "ingest_ts": "2024-11-02T15:23:44Z",
  "provenance": {
    "signed_digest": "sig-v1:base64(...)",
    "signer_id": "kms:service-evidence-ingest",
    "signature_ts": "2024-11-02T15:23:44Z"
  },
  "payload_summary": "short text or JSON snippet (<=512 bytes)",
  "payload_ref": "s3://evidence-staging/<shard>/<key>.ndjson",
  "routing": { "priority": "high|normal|low", "targets": ["siem-east","control-store"] }
}
(Envelope is intentionally small; full payload may be stored in object storage with signed reference).

Fanout semantics and guarantees:
- Exactly-once per-target is the goal; practical implementation: at-least-once delivery with dedupe at sink using evidence_key + signed_digest.
- Fanout workers read ledger entries, hydrate payloads from payload_ref, and push to target with an idempotency header evidence_key.
- If a sink supports idempotency tokens, include evidence_key as idempotency-key.
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter; move to DLQ after N attempts (configurable per target).
- Prioritized fanout: high-priority control events bypass lower-priority batching windows.

Checkpointing, offsets, and idempotency model:
- Evidence Ledger stores (ledger_id, evidence_key, ingest_ts, routing_meta, checkpoint_state).
- Fanout workers commit checkpoints after successful push to all configured targets OR mark partial-success with a per-target status map.
- Checkpoint granularity: per-shard sequence number (e.g., per-collector shard).
- On restart, worker replays from last committed offset and examines evidence_key to avoid duplicate processing.

Backpressure & capacity controls:
- Telemetry Gate enforces per-collector rate limits and global circuit breakers.
- When downstream sinks (SIEM exporters) report high latencies, fanout workers temporarily degrade non-critical targets to deferred-archive and emit an incident metric.
- Batching windows: for cost-sensitive sinks, group low-priority events into 5s windows (configurable).
- Burst protection: short in-memory buffer with soft-limits; when exceeded, Gate responds 429 with Retry-After and persistent queueing is attempted.

Security and chain-of-custody:
- All ingest traffic must use mTLS and RBAC v2 tokens. Collector service roles: collector-ingest, collector-audit (read-only), collector-admin (restricted).
- Provenance signature: Telemetry Gate signs a digest (HMAC-SHA256 or KMS-based) and stores signer_id with signature_ts.
- Evidence payloads stored encrypted at rest with customer key options (KMS keys per-customer for dedicated/private).
- Access controls: control-store exports are only available to roles with explicit evidence-reader scope.

RBAC v2 considerations (practical rules):
- Least privilege: collectors get scoped tokens with allowed evidence types and allowed routes.
- Token rotation and expiry: short-lived tokens (<=30m) for edge collectors; Gate can exchange long-lived certs for short-lived tokens via trusted broker.
- Audit mapping: Gate emits an RBAC-audit record for every token exchange and route decision to support downstream access reviews.

SIEM export mapping guidance (example lines):
- Input envelope -> SIEM event:
  - siem.event_id = evidence_id
  - siem.timestamp = ingest_ts
  - siem.event_type = evidence_type
  - siem.provenance.signature = provenance.signed_digest
  - siem.collector = collector_id
  - siem.payload_summary = payload_summary
- Normalize: map internal severity to SIEM severity (CRITICAL->10, HIGH->7, etc.).
- Events above a severity threshold should carry full payload; below threshold carry summary and payload_ref only.

Export transformation rules and privacy gating:
- PII redaction rules apply before export; Gate applies configurable redaction transforms for exports that cross customer boundaries.
- For customer-owned Dedicated/Private deployments, default export preserves payload unless policy says otherwise.

Operational runbook (top-level steps):
1) Deploy: update Gate config in k8s configmap and roll Gate Deployment with readiness checks.
2) Smoke test: run synthetic event (see test harness section) and verify ledger entry + fanout to test SIEM endpoint.
3) Gradual rollout: canary 5% collectors for 10 minutes -> 25% for 30 minutes -> full. Monitor ingest_errors, fanout_dlq_count, median_latency.
4) Incident: if median_latency > 500ms or DLQ growth > 10/min:
   - Immediately throttle collectors by 50% via Gate policy and escalate to SRE.
   - Enable deferred-archive for non-critical targets and keep only high-priority fanout.
   - Capture a 5-minute evidence snapshot for forensics.
5) Postmortem: attach ledger slices, configuration version, and signer logs to the incident ticket.

Test harness and QA guidance:
- Synthetic generator (repo link in linked_artifacts) can emit realistic control-events and access-events.
- Validation checks: signature verification, evidence_key determinism test, checkpoint replay test, DLQ injection test.
- Fuzzing: randomize payload size and collector_id to test shard balancing.

Example troubleshooting commands (k8s + ledger CLI):
- curl -k -i -X POST https://gate.internal/evidence -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '@sample-envelope.json'
- ledgerctl list --shard s-23 --from 1000 --to 1020
- fanout-worker logs: kubectl logs -l app=fanout-worker -c worker | grep "evidence_key=<hash>"

DLQ and replay strategy:
- DLQ items are stored in an immutable bucket with indexed metadata for quick lookup.
- Operators may replay specific DLQ entries back into the ledger via ledgerctl replay --evidence-key <key>.
- Replay respects original ingest provenance and updates a replay_history field in the ledger metadata.

Metrics and alerts (recommended):
- Metrics: ingest_success_rate, ingest_latency_p50/p95, fanout_success_rate_per_target, dlq_rate_per_target, signature_failure_rate.
- Alerts: p95_ingest_latency > 300ms for 5m, dlq_rate_per_target > 1/min for 10m, signature_failure_rate > 0.1% for 5m.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Decide final envelope v2 vs v2.1 fields for cross-customer correlation (Priya to propose).
- Validate per-customer KMS signer integration for Dedicated path (security team).
- Performance target: confirm 100ms SLA for small control events under 50k rps ingress (SRE capacity modeling needed).
- Define canonical SIEM field mapping JSON and add to Confluence (Diego).

Appendix: sample raw entry (ndjson line) for ledger storage:
{"ledger_id":"s-23:1000123","evidence_key":"sha256:abc123...","collector_id":"edge-23","ingest_ts":"2024-11-02T15:23:44Z","routing":"siem-east,control-store","payload_ref":"s3://evidence-staging/s-23/1000123.ndjson","status":"pending"}

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: it mixes the design spec with runbook steps to help teams implement quickly. Please comment inline for policy decisions (redaction, retention) and escalate any regulatory constraints that require per-customer customization.
- If you are integrating a new SIEM, add it to linked_artifacts and create a small compatibility shim in the fanout layer.

Revision history:
